Observed learning · 2026-10-28 · seeds 2/3/4

Franka cable lift: fresh seeds and an action-gain control

Stock RSL-RL PPO, native CUDA PPO, pristine authors’ compiled Torch FlashSAC AMP and native CUDA FlashSAC AMP in the same coupled rigid-body/cable task.

Study question. Do the earlier learning patterns persist in fresh seeds after merging current main, and does a larger policy-to-task action gain change the official Torch SAC outcome? The primary study contains 12 runs, 589,824,000 training transitions and 108 common evaluations. Each run collects 49,152,000 transitions. A separately audited control, when included, contributes two official Torch runs and 18 evaluations; its results remain separate.

Observed outcomes

Stock RSL-RL PPO: final ever-goal 92.19–99.22% and final-hold 52.34–94.53% across the three observed seeds. Native CUDA PPO: final ever-goal 91.41–97.66% and final-hold 78.91–96.09% across the three observed seeds. Official Torch FlashSAC AMP: final ever-goal 0.00–0.00% and final-hold 0.00–0.00% across the three observed seeds. Native CUDA FlashSAC AMP: final ever-goal 0.00–0.00% and final-hold 0.00–0.00% across the three observed seeds.

These are ranges of observed seed outcomes. Every checkpoint and run is retained below. No population task-solved threshold, significance claim or equivalent-quality assumption is introduced.

What the task metrics mean

Ever goal means cable segment 6 came strictly within 5 cm of its commanded XYZ at least once; grasp or contact is not an additional condition. Occupancy divides successful active states by the full 128×150 budget, with zero remaining success after an early failure. Final hold requires an episode to remain active through the final 15 scored steps and stay within the goal throughout them. Lift is a separate diagnostic: the middle segment exceeded 5 cm world/environment-relative height at least once. It is not the stock success definition.

All checkpoints, including iteration 0, use the same 128 complete physical states and goals, world/cable gravity −9.81 m/s² and final action-rate penalty −0.1. The stock arm remains gravity-disabled. The first termination or timeout ends scoring for an episode; autoreset trajectories do not contribute. Returns are evaluated under this final curriculum and are not training-reward averages.

Task quality beside execution time

Production process clocks use shared on-disk compiler caches warmed by fixtures and the preceding smokes. They include worker imports, environment construction, cache loading, collection, learning, metrics and checkpoint writes; they are not total cold-start allocation costs. Startup components, the nested training loop, final full replay IO and the complete evaluator are shown as distinct scopes. Their overlapping costs must not be summed. Different learned trajectories and reset frequencies can change collection time, so the full process cost cannot establish an isolated kernel-speed effect.

These actual parent command clocks separate all four smokes from production. The final column includes intervening root-gate waits. Source transfer, package installation and fixture generation precede the first smoke and are outside this scope; a cold bootstrap total is not inferred from these values. The first official Torch smoke can compile/autotune while later workers reuse caches. Smoke order, physics-cache state and recipe differ together, so their times do not isolate cold compiler performance. Per-iteration collection/learning diagnostics are host dispatch and synchronization scopes, not pure steady GPU update or rollout latency.

Action and reward diagnostics

Training action statistics describe sampled policy outputs in normalized replay coordinates, before any gain. Evaluation action statistics describe deterministic outputs. Neither an action magnitude threshold nor the configured target entropy scale measures physical actuator saturation or actual exploration coverage. Reward terms are recorded before SAC reward normalization; actor/temperature metrics retain the last available value per key in an iteration, rather than an average over updates.

SAC update signals

Reading the SAC signals. The learned coefficient α weights entropy in the actor loss; it does not directly multiply rollout noise. Negative differential entropy is valid. For 8 actions, the authors’ Gaussian-reference σ=0.15 gives a target of −3.82545 nats; σ is not a measured rollout standard deviation. Replay rewards are divided by a scale built from running discounted-reward statistics and a historical magnitude bound. These persistent statistics can interact with curricula, but this study does not establish a failure cause. Source: entropy target, temperature update and reward scaling.

Separate official Torch action-gain control

Two additional official Torch runs use seeds 2/3 on allocation D. The gain 1 references below are the corresponding primary runs, reused as references without adding them to the primary population. D uses the repaired consumer source to forward the parent allocation to worker subprocesses. Its only changed source files are that argument forwarding and a changelog note; the 38 learner library files and package metadata remain byte-identical. Its canonical fixture producer remains the original primary source, with all 12 files unchanged.

The control multiplies all 8 policy action dimensions by 3 before the unchanged task action manager. An arm offset can therefore reach ±0.09 rad per control step instead of ±0.03 rad for tanh outputs; gripper limit clipping and action-dependent reward terms can also change. Replay, density and entropy calculations stay in normalized policy coordinates. This is one configured wrapper factor with several downstream effects. A change in learning does not prove an arm-range, gripper, reward or exploration mechanism. Device, chronology, cache history and stochastic trajectories also differ between the reference and control runs.

How to interpret PPO seed and backend differences

Initial model and normalization arrays match exactly within each algorithm/seed pair, but complete random trajectories are not coupled. Stock Torch PPO and native PPO use different sampling and minibatch RNG paths; Torch permits TF32 while native dense math is strict FP32. Floating-point reduction order can also differ. Those differences can change actions, contacts, resets and subsequent training data in a coupled task. They are plausible contributors to seed/backend variability; this study does not isolate each cause.

The native PPO adapter uses actual RSL 5.5.1 EmpiricalNormalization semantics, updating after the full PPO update and freezing buffers during evaluation. Physical checkpoints audit those buffers and actual optimizer steps. PPO retains the stock [256,128,64] ELU network, unclipped Gaussian actions and γ=0.98. FlashSAC uses the authors’ architecture/losses with γ=0.99, compiled FP16 AMP for official Torch, and FP16 dense operands with FP32 accumulation/outputs/master/adjoint/Adam state for native CUDA. Intermediate rounding, scaler skips and RNG trajectories can differ.

Replay and curriculum hypotheses

Both SAC backends use 10M replay, 100,000-transition warmup, batch 2048, one-step returns and a fixed 12,800-update learning-rate decay for each optimizer, counted by its update calls. The configured target sigma 0.15 is an entropy target parameter, not a measured rollout standard deviation. Replay can mix samples collected under changing gravity and action-rate curricula. Action range, entropy/temperature dynamics, reward normalization and that nonstationarity are hypotheses to inspect alongside the logged curves; no failure mechanism is established by these observations. This is an adapted cable recipe, not an authors-published cable configuration.

Methods and limits

The registered Isaac-Lift-Cable-Franka state task has 69 observations and 8 actions. Primary runs use 1024 environments × 24 steps × 2000 iterations. Newton MJWarp rigid physics and VBD cable physics exchange rigid-body proxies; physics capture and native learning capture are separate graphs. The three primary cohorts use seeds 2/3/4 on allocations A/B/C and the first three frozen Williams rows. Position and predecessor effects are not fully balanced; seed, GPU and chronology vary together. Earlier workers and smokes warm shared caches. There is no independent repeat of each seed on another device.

Canonical fixtures include scene poses/velocities, targets, action and command buffers, clocks, gravity and sticky reward state. Saved physical/manager hashes and raw initial observation hashes match every evaluation. Public scene restore cold-resets solver history; hidden solver buffers and global RNG trajectories are not serialized. All six primary SAC final continuations preserve full replay, optimizers and scaler state, separately from portable evaluation checkpoints. Native replay adds one FP32 discount per transition. Actual completions/skips are decoded from checkpoint payloads; smoke perturb/reload/continuation and production are distinct evidence.

Oct 27 seeds 0/1 used the older coherent Isaac/Newton/runtime stack. The present source merges upstream main and keeps the stream-owner repair; task recipe/geometry remain checked, while engine/runtime dependencies changed. Historical outcomes are not pooled with these new cohorts. Earlier study.
